reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: Second most common type 1 CDG after PMM2-CDG, caused by biallelic ALG6 variants
Generally milder than PMM2-CDG, with developmental delay, hypotonia and epilepsy predominating
Cerebellar hypoplasia is typically less prominent than in PMM2-CDG
Features may include failure to thrive, feeding difficulties, and a coagulopathy with low antithrombin and protein C/S
Some patients have retinopathy, deep vein thrombosis or ichthyosiform skin changes; virilisation/genital anomalies have been described
Serum transferrin analysis shows a type 1 pattern reflecting loss of whole N-glycan chains at the assembly stage
Definitive diagnosis rests on lipid-linked oligosaccharide analysis and ALG6 gene sequencing
Management is supportive and multidisciplinary; no proven disease-modifying therapy exists
reference.pathophysiology: ALG6-CDG is a defect in the endoplasmic reticulum assembly of the lipid-linked oligosaccharide precursor used for N-glycosylation. The ALG6 enzyme is the dolichyl-phosphate glucosyltransferase that adds the first glucose residue to the Man9GlcNAc2 dolichol-linked structure. When this step is impaired, an incompletely glucosylated precursor is transferred less efficiently to nascent proteins, producing hypoglycosylation with loss of complete glycan chains and hence a type 1 serum transferrin pattern. As with other N-glycosylation defects the deficiency affects multiple organ systems, but the neurological phenotype tends to be less severe than PMM2-CDG. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.
additionalDifferentials: PMM2-CDG and other type 1 CDGs (shared transferrin screening pattern)
additionalInvestigations: Serum transferrin isoelectric focusing/mass spectrometry (type 1 pattern)
Coagulation panel including antithrombin, protein C and protein S
Brain MRI and EEG for epilepsy and structural anomalies
redFlags: Poorly controlled or status epilepticus in infancy
Thromboembolic events including deep vein thrombosis
Acute metabolic or systemic deterioration during intercurrent illness
Progressive failure to thrive with feeding failure
reference.prognosis: The phenotype is generally milder than PMM2-CDG with better survival, but most patients have persisting intellectual disability, epilepsy and variable multisystem involvement.
pitfalls: Stopping the workup at the transferrin screen without identifying the specific CDG subtype
Neonatal or infection-related false transferrin patterns misleading interpretation
Overlooking coagulation abnormalities before surgery or anticoagulation
Assuming a benign course given the milder label and under-monitoring multisystem complications
Missing retinopathy or thrombotic risk on long-term follow-up
references: Scriver's Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease (OMMBID)
Jaeken J, Inborn Errors of Metabolism: Diagnosis and Treatment
